examples.en: I bought a reddish-brown leather bag.
A dark brown coat suits autumn well.
The fallen leaves turned reddish brown.

examples.ko: 이 소파는 짙은 고동색이라 때가 잘 안 보여요.
examples.en: This sofa is a deep brown, so dirt doesn't show much.
What socks would go well with brown shoes?
I dyed my hair a reddish brown.

explain: 갈색 중에서도 짙고 붉은 기가 도는 색을 말해요. 일상에서는 그냥 '갈색'이라고도 많이 해요. 가죽, 나무, 낙엽 같은 것의 색을 말할 때 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is a dark brown with a reddish tint. In daily talk people often just say '갈색'. It suits describing the color of leather, wood or fallen leaves.

examples.en: My grandmother's life was truly hard and unlucky.
He's a person born to an unfortunate fate.

examples.ko: 드라마 속 주인공의 인생이 너무 기구해요.
examples.en: The drama's main character's life is so unlucky.
I heard the story of a life lived with great misfortune.
I didn't know my fate would be this unfortunate.
His life was so unfortunate that it hurt my heart.

explain: 하루 일이 안 풀린 정도가 아니라, 인생이나 운명이 계속 힘들고 순탄하지 않을 때 써요. '불행하다'보다 문학적이고 이야기에 어울려요. 주로 '기구한 운명', '기구한 삶', '기구한 인생'처럼 짝으로 나와요.
explain_en: It is not for a bad day but for a life or fate that keeps being hard and bumpy. It is more literary than 불행하다 and fits stories. It mostly appears in set pairs: 기구한 운명, 기구한 삶, 기구한 인생.

examples.en: The book cover has come apart completely in tatters.
The knees of the jeans are ripped to shreds.

examples.ko: 너덜너덜 낡은 가방을 아직도 메고 다녀요.
examples.en: I still carry around that worn-out, tattered bag.
The old flag is blowing in the wind in tatters.

examples.ko: 사전이 너덜너덜 헤질 만큼 많이 봤어요.
examples.en: I used the dictionary so much that it fell apart.
The clothes were worn to rags, so I threw them away.

explain: '너덜거리다'가 늘어져 흔들리는 동작이라면 '너덜너덜'은 해지고 찢어진 모양 자체를 보여 줘요. '찢어지다, 해지다, 낡다' 같은 말과 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: '너덜거리다' is the swinging motion of something hanging loose, while '너덜너덜' shows the torn, frayed look itself. It goes well with words like '찢어지다', '해지다' and '낡다'.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 몸집은 작아도 정말 다부져요.
examples.en: That player is small but really tough.
I walked into the interview room with a determined look.
My younger sibling made up their mind firmly and started studying.

examples.ko: 아이가 말하는 게 어찌나 다부진지 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: The child spoke so firmly that I was surprised.

examples.ko: 다부져 보이는 체격이라 운동을 오래 했나 봐요.
examples.en: He has a sturdy build, so he must have exercised for a long time.
The youngest is known for being tough, so I do not worry.

explain: '튼튼하다'는 건강하고 잘 망가지지 않는 느낌이고, '다부지다'는 몸이나 태도가 꽉 짜여서 약해 보이지 않는 느낌이에요. '야무지다'는 일 처리가 빈틈없을 때 더 잘 어울려요. 몸집이 작은데 의외로 단단하거나 어린 사람이 당찰 때도 써요. 칭찬하는 말이에요.
explain_en: '튼튼하다' suggests healthy and not easily broken, while '다부지다' suggests a body or attitude that is tightly built and does not look weak. '야무지다' fits better when someone handles tasks without gaps. It also fits a small person who is surprisingly solid, or a young person who is spirited. It is a compliment.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 박진감이 넘쳐서 시간이 빨리 갔어요.
examples.en: This movie is so thrilling that time flew by.

examples.ko: 박진감 있는 경기라서 끝까지 숨죽이고 봤어요.
examples.en: It was such an exciting game that I watched it holding my breath.
The music adds a sense of excitement to the scene.
It has a lot of excitement, but the story is a little weak.

examples.ko: 박진감에 빠져서 시간 가는 줄 몰랐어요.
examples.en: I got caught up in the thrill and lost track of time.
The director captivated the audience with intensity.

explain: 영화, 경기, 게임이 생생하고 빠르게 진행되어 실제처럼 느껴질 때 써요. '박진감 넘치다', '박진감이 있다'가 자주 쓰여요. '긴장감'은 조마조마한 마음이고, '박진감'은 장면이 살아 움직이는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is used when a movie, game or match moves fast and vividly so it feels real. Common forms are '박진감 넘치다' and '박진감이 있다'. '긴장감' is the nervous feeling, while '박진감' is the sense that the scene is alive and moving.

examples.ko: 새로 지은 성은 웅장한 위용을 자랑해요.
examples.en: The newly built castle shows off its grand, imposing look.

examples.ko: 큰 배가 항구에 들어오는 위용에 모두 놀랐어요.
examples.en: Everyone was amazed at the imposing sight of the big ship entering the port.
That mountain overwhelms people with its majesty alone.
Its grandeur was so impressive that I looked up at it for a long time.

examples.ko: 오랜 공사 끝에 다리가 위용을 드러냈어요.
examples.en: After a long construction period, the bridge revealed its grand form.

examples.ko: 위용 있는 건물 앞에서 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: I took a photo in front of the imposing building.

explain: '위엄'은 사람이나 행동에서 느껴지는 점잖은 권위 쪽이고, '위용'은 큰 건물, 산, 배, 군대처럼 겉모습이 당당하고 웅장한 느낌이에요. '위용을 자랑하다/드러내다/뽐내다'처럼 짝지어 써요.
explain_en: '위엄' leans toward the dignified authority felt in a person or their behavior, while '위용' is about the grand, commanding outward appearance of big things like buildings, mountains, ships, or armies. It pairs with '위용을 자랑하다/드러내다/뽐내다'.

examples.ko: 친구 부모님이 저를 융숭하게 대접해 주셨어요.
examples.en: My friend's parents treated me very warmly.

examples.ko: 융숭한 대접을 받아서 오히려 몸 둘 바를 몰랐어요.
examples.en: I received such generous hospitality that I didn't know where to put myself.

examples.ko: 손님을 융숭하게 맞이하는 것이 우리 집 전통이에요.
examples.en: Welcoming guests warmly is a tradition in our family.

examples.ko: 집 앞에서 융숭한 환영을 받고 감동했어요.
examples.en: I was moved by the warm welcome I got in front of the house.

examples.ko: 대접이 너무 융숭해서 감사 인사를 여러 번 했어요.
examples.en: The hospitality was so generous that I thanked them several times.
I felt good because I was treated so generously.

explain: 주로 '대접', '환영', '대우' 같은 말과 함께 '융숭한 대접'처럼 덩어리로 써요. 비슷한 말로 '극진하다'가 있어요. 손님을 정성껏 맞이하는 장면에서 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is mostly used in chunks with words like '대접' (treatment), '환영' (welcome) and '대우' (treatment), as in '융숭한 대접'. A similar word is '극진하다'. It fits scenes where guests are received with great care.

examples.en: A silence hung in the room for a moment.

examples.ko: 새벽 거리의 적막을 깨고 오토바이가 지나갔어요.
examples.en: A motorcycle passed, breaking the stillness of the dawn street.

examples.ko: 사람들이 모두 떠나자 마을은 적막에 잠겼어요.
examples.en: When everyone left, the village sank into stillness.

examples.ko: 적막 속에서 시계 소리만 크게 들렸어요.
examples.en: In the silence, only the sound of the clock was loud.
I disliked the silence, so I left the TV on.

examples.ko: 눈 내린 밤의 적막은 오히려 편안해요.
examples.en: The stillness of a snowy night is rather comforting.

explain: '침묵'은 말을 안 하는 것이고 '고요'는 조용한 상태인데, '적막'은 조용한 데다 쓸쓸한 느낌까지 있어요. '적막이 흐르다, 감돌다'처럼 말하고 글에서 더 자주 보여요.
explain_en: '침묵' is not speaking and '고요' is a calm quiet state, but '적막' is quiet with a touch of loneliness. You say '적막이 흐르다' or '적막이 감돌다', and it appears more often in writing.

examples.en: Even after making a mistake, he smiled as if nothing had happened.
Even while lying, he had an unruffled expression.

examples.ko: 왜 그렇게 태연스러워요? 걱정도 안 돼요?
examples.en: Why are you so unfazed? Aren't you worried?

examples.ko: 저렇게 태연스러워 보여도 속으로는 떨고 있을 거예요.
examples.en: Even though he looks that cool, he's probably shaking inside.

examples.ko: 제 친구는 큰 사고 소식에도 너무 태연스러워서 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was surprised that my friend was so calm even at news of a big accident.
I tried to act calm, but my hands shook.

explain: '태연하다'와 뜻이 거의 같아서 바꿔 써도 돼요. 'ㅂ' 불규칙이라 '태연스러워요', '태연스러운'으로 바뀌어요. 보통 걱정하거나 놀랄 만한 상황에서 아무렇지 않은 듯한 모습을 말해요.
explain_en: It means nearly the same as '태연하다', so the two can be swapped. It is a ㅂ-irregular adjective, so it becomes '태연스러워요' and '태연스러운'. It usually describes someone acting unbothered in a situation where you would expect worry or surprise.

examples.en: In this hot weather, my back is soaked with sweat.
The cup tipped over and the floor was covered in water.
I got rained on, and the inside of my shoes is sopping wet.
I sweated until my palms were drenched.

examples.ko: 흥건한 땀을 닦고 시원한 물을 마셨어요.
examples.en: I wiped off the dripping sweat and drank some cold water.
The frozen meat thawed and the plate became full of liquid.

explain: 물이나 땀 같은 액체가 고이거나 푹 젖어서 많이 있는 상태예요. '땀으로 흥건하다'처럼 '-으로'와 함께 쓰는 경우가 많아요. 그냥 '젖다'보다 액체가 눈에 띄게 많은 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It describes a state where a lot of liquid, such as water or sweat, has pooled or soaked in. It often takes '-으로', as in '땀으로 흥건하다'. Compared with plain '젖다' (to get wet), it gives the feeling that there is visibly a lot of liquid.
